coreIdea: Decidable = algorithm always halts with correct answer. Rice's Theorem: any non-trivial semantic property of a TM's LANGUAGE is undecidable. DFA questions usually decidable; CFG/TM semantic questions usually undecidable.
mustRememberFormulas: Rice's Theorem: non-trivial property of L(M) → undecidable, for arbitrary TM M
L Recursive ⟺ L and complement(L) both RE
Decidable: DFA/PDA/CFG membership, emptiness, finiteness, DFA equivalence
Undecidable: CFG ambiguity, CFG equivalence, CFG universality (=Σ*), CFL∩CFL emptiness, TM halting (any form)

commonTrapsQuickList: Rice's Theorem applies to LANGUAGE (semantic) properties, NOT structural/syntactic ones (like state count)
DFA questions ≈ always decidable; the SAME question about a CFG or TM is often undecidable
NP ⊆ Decidable — NP is about efficiency, not decidability itself
Reduce FROM the known-undecidable problem TO the target, not the reverse
highYieldPyqLessons: Problem classification (17/30) is the dominant skill — build fluency with the decidable/undecidable list across DFA/CFG/TM, and internalize Rice's Theorem as the single most powerful shortcut.
This is the natural TOC capstone — every prior topic (Regular, FA, CFL, PDA, Identify Class) feeds directly into recognizing WHY a given problem is or isn't decidable.
